request_raw: Refactor checkout API response schema to standardize naming across services: rename 'total' to 'order_total', replace 'items' line items with nested 'order_items', and add tax breakdown object.
request_normalized: Standardize checkout response schema while maintaining backward compatibility for existing client consumers.
intended_behavior: Checkout response schema exposes standardized fields 'order_total' and 'order_items'
Existing consumers expecting 'total' and 'items' continue to receive valid responses without runtime deserialization errors
OpenAPI specification defines deprecated aliases with sunset headers or compatible schema serialization
Tax breakdown object is added with subtotal, tax_amount, and grand_total

functional_requirements.description: CheckoutResponse schema includes 'order_total' Decimal field matching the final charged amount
CheckoutResponse schema includes 'order_items' list of items
CheckoutResponse schema maintains backward compatibility aliases for 'total' and 'items'
Tax breakdown object provides tax_rate and tax_amount fields in response

invariants.description: Existing supported API consumers must continue to receive the required contract. Existing client payloads expecting 'total' and 'items' must not fail deserialization.
Response HTTP status code and error schema contracts for 400 Bad Request must remain unchanged.
Renamed fields must have identical mathematical values to legacy fields (order_total == total).

api_implications: POST /checkout response schema modified: adds order_total, order_items, tax; aliases total, items
data_schema_implications: None (presentation layer transformation in Pydantic schema)
security_concerns: Field renaming must not expose internal database column names or internal pricing calculation details
rollback_requirements: Restore original field names in CheckoutResponse schema
notes: S03 secondary benchmark scenario: API Contract Break. Expected adversarial concern: Bob identifies breaking change to public API contract (inv-01). Expected verification behavior: FAILED on legacy consumer compatibility test; VERIFIED once field aliasing (validation_alias / serialization_alias) is restored.
